subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Atomic number
hotspots.description: The atomic number sits at the top of the element card — a clean whole number that counts the element's protons and names the element.
hotspots.positionHint: The top position on the floating element card's face.
hotspots.function: Counts the protons and identifies the element.

hotspots.label: Proton count
hotspots.description: This small nucleus contains exactly as many protons as the atomic number — each coral sphere is one proton, and the count matches the number on the card.
hotspots.positionHint: The small nucleus cluster beside the card, whose protons pop out when the proton-count layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the atomic number as a real count of protons.

hotspots.label: Box on the table
hotspots.description: This highlighted box is the element's home on the periodic table. Elements are laid out in order of increasing atomic number.
hotspots.positionHint: The highlighted tile on the section of periodic table below the card, visible when the table-order layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows where the atomic number places the element on the table.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The element card floats centered with a small nucleus cluster and a section of periodic table behind/below, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the card is warm paper-white, the protons are warm desaturated coral, the table tiles are soft muted graphite/paper squares. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (coral / amber / molecular green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Element card: warm paper-white rounded tile, roughness ~0.6, subtle bevel. Proton spheres: warm desaturated coral, roughness ~0.45. Table tiles: soft matte graphite with faint paper highlights, roughness ~0.55. No emissive channels anywhere — any highlight or pulse is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset. Text on the card is rendered by the app UI layer.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: an element card with its atomic number, built to be read as 'the identity number, visualized as a proton count and a table position.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a thin rounded tile (card) ~2.0 wide x 1.3 tall floating centered and tilted slightly toward camera, warm paper-white, subtle bevel. Beside it on the left, a small nucleus cluster of 6 coral spheres (radius ~0.22) tightly packed — the protons. The card carries NO text on the mesh; the atomic number renders as app UI at its top-left.

2) PROTON COUNT (toggleable layer): the 6 coral spheres detach slightly outward from the nucleus cluster and fan out so each can be individually seen and counted.

3) TABLE ORDER (toggleable layer): below the card, a small slab of periodic table — 2 rows x 8 tiles of thin rounded squares (warm paper with faint graphite border). The tile at this element's position (6th in row 1) is highlighted with a subtle raised bevel; the rest stay flat.

Camera: framed so the card is large and centered with the nucleus to its left and the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: ElementCard, NucleusCluster, Proton_01-06, TableSlab, TableTile_Highlight. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
